title: Video Streaming Platform
summary: Build a YouTube-scale platform: upload once, transcode asynchronously, and stream globally from the edge.
narrative:
This is the capstone. A creator uploads a two-hour 4K file from a laptop in Berlin; minutes later a viewer in Sao Paulo taps play and it starts instantly at whatever quality their connection can handle. Between those two moments sits nearly every pattern you have learned so far, assembled into one system.

Start with two paths that must never interfere. API calls enter through a load balancer and an API gateway into redundant web servers; metadata lives in SQL with a hot-row cache. Support chunked, resumable multipart uploads. Presigned URLs commonly let clients upload parts straight to object storage, but this level chooses an app-mediated upload proxy to preserve its no-direct-storage rule: the web tier streams each chunk into an object-store multipart upload without buffering whole videos. The Web Server → Blob Storage edge represents that transfer. Validate completion before queuing a transcode job.

The queue feeds transcoding workers that write an HLS/DASH bitrate ladder, manifests and segments back to Blob Storage. Publish playable metadata only when the required renditions are ready. Playback follows Client → CDN → Blob Storage; the player switches bitrate segments based on bandwidth and buffer occupancy. Upload, transcode and playback remain independent so a backlog never stalls existing playback. Watch-time, engagement and abandonment events can use the Message Queue → Stream Processor bonus branch for analytics; Monitoring tracks operational health.

functional: Accept chunked, resumable multipart uploads through the app tier into durable object storage
Transcode asynchronously into an HLS/DASH bitrate ladder and write manifests/segments back to Blob Storage
Stream from the CDN with adaptive bitrate selection based on bandwidth and buffer occupancy
Store and serve video metadata for browse and playback
nonFunctional: Playback starts fast for viewers anywhere on Earth
A transcode backlog never blocks uploads or playback
The metadata API survives the loss of any single app server
constraints: API traffic enters through the load balancer and gateway only
Clients never touch object storage directly: this level proxies upload parts through the app tier and serves playback through the CDN
Every API call is routed and authorized by the gateway
capacity: ~500 hours of video uploaded per minute
specs.tradeoff: Decoupling transcoding behind a queue trades immediate availability of a new upload for an ingest path that never stalls under load. App-mediated uploads enforce this level's storage boundary but consume app bandwidth; direct presigned client uploads are a common alternative outside this topology. A larger bitrate ladder raises storage/encoding cost while improving playback across diverse connections.
specs.bonus: Add Monitoring & Alerting to watch transcode queue depth, CDN hit ratio, and playback errors. Stream watch-time, engagement and abandonment events from the Message Queue to a Stream Processor.

topologyRules.message: API traffic enters through the Load Balancer and Gateway, never straight to a Web Server.
Clients never touch object storage directly; playback goes through the CDN and uploads through the app tier.
Every API call must be routed and authorized by the API Gateway before it reaches the app tier.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two Web Servers so the metadata API survives the loss of any single instance.
Front Blob Storage with a CDN, or global playback will crush the origin.

hints: Split the system in two: an API path (Client -> Load Balancer -> API Gateway -> Web Server) for metadata and uploads, and a playback path (Client -> CDN -> Blob Storage) for watching.

Stream resumable upload parts through Web Server → Blob Storage in this level; direct Client → Blob Storage is forbidden. Wire Web Server → Message Queue → two Workers, then each Worker → Blob Storage for encoded HLS/DASH renditions.

Front Blob Storage with the CDN for global delivery, cache hot metadata, keep the SQL Database as the source of truth, and run at least two Web Servers. Wire Message Queue → Stream Processor for watch-time analytics and each Web Server → Monitoring.
tips: How would you design the video upload pipeline - how is the video received, stored, and encoded into multiple resolutions?
How do you store videos? Object store like S3 or HDFS?
How do you ensure low-latency, high-availability playback across the globe? Would you use a CDN or edge caching?
What analytics do you track (watch time, engagement, abandonment)? How is it processed?
